title: Resolve a JSON Pointer
statement:
Write a JavaScript function `resolvePointer(doc, pointer)` that evaluates a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) against a JSON value.

Rules:
- `doc` is any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean or null).
- The empty pointer `""` refers to the whole document.
- Any other pointer must start with `/`. It is split on `/` into reference tokens; each token is unescaped by replacing `~1` with `/` and then `~0` with `~`. A `~` followed by anything other than `0` or `1` (or at the end of a token) makes the pointer invalid.
- On an object, a token selects the member with exactly that name (an own property; names are case-sensitive, and the empty string is a valid name).
- On an array, a token must be a non-negative integer in decimal with no leading zeros (`0`, `7`, `12`, but not `01`, `-1`, `1.0` or `-`); it selects that index if it is inside the array.
- Anything else, including stepping into a string, number, boolean or null, means the target does not exist.
- Return `{ "found": true, "value": <the value> }` when the target exists, and `{ "found": false }` when it does not.
- Return `null` when the pointer is not a string, does not start with `/` (unless empty), or contains an invalid `~` escape.
